interface.title: Oligo Analyzer Pro (v1.0.0, Bio-Tools Suite)
interface.stage_of_work: Checking candidate primers before ordering them for synthesis
interface.what_it_is_for: Gives the Wallace-rule Tm, GC%, AT%, molecular weight, base composition and reverse complement for one pasted primer, or for every record in an uploaded FASTA/txt file, with a GC% vs Tm scatter plot and a CSV report.

data.note: The Single Sequence tab used sequences I typed in: ATGCGTACGTTAGCCTAGGC (balanced), atatatatgcnatatat (AT-rich, lowercase, with an N) and atatatatgcnxatat (invalid). The Bulk tab used sample_primers.fasta, 8 records including deliberate outliers: a high-GC primer, a low-Tm primer, a 4-mer, a 60-mer and one with an N. It also includes forward/reverse pairs for GAPDH and TP53. I checked the Tm, GC% and reverse complement by hand for the first sequence, and they are correct.

features.name: Sequence property calculator with metric cards
features.general: Enter one sequence, check that it only uses allowed characters, and show a row of headline numbers for it with a target-range hint
features.specific: Paste DNA (5'→3'), press Analyze, and read the Tm (Wallace rule, with a 'Target: 55-60°C' pill that differs from the help panel's 50-60 °C and shows whatever the Tm is), GC Content, AT Content and Mol Wt cards; invalid characters give a red 'INVALID SEQUENCE DETECTED!' alert, which allows A, T, G, C or N although the input tooltip says only A, T, C, G
steps: Type or paste a sequence into the input field (lowercase is accepted)
Press Analyze (Enter only commits the text)
Read the four metric cards and compare Tm with the target pill
If an invalid character is entered, read the error and fix the input
serves_tasks: Compute the key physical properties of one sequence and judge whether it is usable
Repeat the check for another item, including bad input

features.name: Composition bar chart with data-table toggle
features.general: Show how often each symbol occurs in one item as a bar chart, and switch to the underlying counts table
features.specific: The Nucleotide Composition chart gives A/C/G/T counts; 'Show data' turns it into a Nucleotide/Count table and the chart icon turns it back. The chart is the tool's own; the 'Show data' toolbar comes from Streamlit's standard chart element, not from this tool.
steps: Analyze a sequence so the chart is drawn
Compare bar heights for skew (for example, A and T at 7 while C and G are at 1)
Press 'Show data' to see the exact counts
Press the chart icon to return to the bars
serves_tasks: Check the composition of one sequence to see if it is skewed

features.name: Derived-sequence block with copy button
features.general: Show a sequence computed from the input in a monospace block that copies to the clipboard in one click, ready to paste into an order form
features.specific: The Reverse Complement code block shows the 5'-3' reverse complement; hovering shows a copy icon that puts the sequence on the clipboard
steps: Analyze a sequence
Hover the Reverse Complement block
Click the copy icon and paste the sequence into an order
serves_tasks: Get the reverse complement of a sequence to order

features.name: Batch file upload into a per-record results table
features.general: Upload a multi-record text file, compute the same properties for every record, and confirm how many were processed; removing the file clears all results
features.specific: Bulk Analysis uploader (.fasta/.txt, 200MB) shows 'Successfully processed N sequences', then the plot, Data Table and Download Report button; ⊗ removes the file and resets the tab. According to the reviewer's reading of app.py, records with characters other than A/T/G/C/N or with empty sequences are dropped without any message, so N is the only clue (not tested in this run).
steps: Click Upload and choose a FASTA/txt file
Read the success message and check that its count matches the number of records in the file
Review the plot and table that appear below
Remove the file with ⊗ to clear and start again
serves_tasks: Load a batch file and compute properties for every record
Clear the batch to start again

features.name: Interactive outlier scatter plot
features.general: Plot every item by two properties, coloured by a third, to spot outliers; hover for values, zoom with the wheel, drag to pan, double-click to reset, open fullscreen and export a PNG
features.specific: The Batch Quality Control plot shows GC% vs Tm (C), coloured by Length; tooltips give GC%/Tm/Length (no primer ID). The plot itself is the tool's; zoom/pan/reset and the toolbar (Show data, Download as PNG, Copy Vega-Lite spec, Fullscreen) come from Streamlit's Vega-Lite chart element, not from this tool, and the tool does not mark or filter outliers.
steps: Look for points far from the main cluster (Tm 180, Tm 12, GC 0, GC 90)
Hover a point to read its GC%, Tm and Length
Zoom with the wheel and drag to pan around the cluster
Double-click to reset the view
Open Fullscreen and press 'Download as PNG' to save the figure
serves_tasks: Spot outlier items on a two-property scatter plot
Save the plot as an image

features.name: Sortable, searchable results grid with column statistics
features.general: Rank items by any property, find items by name, hide columns you don't need, and see summary statistics with a histogram for a numeric column
features.specific: The Data Table (ID, Length, Tm (C), GC%, AT%, MW (Da), Sequence, Rev_Comp) holds the tool's results. Header sorting, Search, Show/hide columns and the column menu's Statistics (mean, SD, percentiles, histogram) are all built into Streamlit's dataframe grid, not added by this tool.
steps: Click a column header, or open its menu and choose Sort ascending/descending
Press Search and type part of an ID to highlight the matching rows
Press Show/hide columns and untick the columns to hide
Open a numeric column's menu and choose Statistics
serves_tasks: Rank and look up items in the results table

features.name: CSV report export
features.general: Download the full per-item results table as a CSV file for records or ordering
features.specific: '📥 Download Report' saves oligo_batch_results.csv with ID, Length, Tm (C), GC%, AT%, MW (Da), Sequence and Rev_Comp, in file order
steps: Upload a batch and check the results
Press '📥 Download Report'
Open the CSV (the table's sort order and hidden columns are not applied)
serves_tasks: Export the batch results as a report

features.name: Collapsible guidance panel with acceptance ranges
features.general: Keep the interpretation ranges for the computed properties in a collapsible help panel beside the input, so the user can judge results against them
features.specific: The '📖 How to use this tool' expander gives 'Tm (Melting Temp): Aim for 50-60°C' and 'GC%: Ideal range is usually 40-60%'; a ? tooltip on the input says 'Only A, T, C, G characters allowed.'
steps: Click '📖 How to use this tool' to open the panel
Read the Tm and GC% ranges
Hover the ? icon by the input to see which characters are allowed
Use the ranges to judge the metric cards or the batch table
serves_tasks: Read the acceptance criteria used to judge a candidate

screens_never_reached: Streamlit Main menu (⋮) and Deploy: these are framework controls, not part of the scientific interface, so I did not open them
Sidebar LinkedIn, GitHub and Email links: they point off-site or to '#', and pages outside 127.0.0.1:8501 do not load
not_done: The data grid's own 'Download as CSV' toolbar button saved no file in this browser (screens/030.webp); only the app's 'Download Report' button produced a CSV
I could not tell which primer a scatter-plot point is from the plot itself, because the tooltip shows only GC%, Tm and Length, not the ID. I matched points to primers through the Data Table instead

The README says the plot can flag outliers, but the app does not mark or filter them; the scientist has to judge by eye. The Tm target pill always shows '↑ Target: 55-60°C' whatever the Tm is (62 °C and 36 °C both showed it)
The ranges disagree: the 'How to use this tool' panel says aim for Tm 50-60 °C (screens/003.webp), while the Tm pill says 55-60 °C (screens/005.webp)
The allowed characters disagree: the input tooltip says 'Only A, T, C, G characters allowed' (screens/004.webp), but N is accepted (screens/014.webp) and the invalid-input alert lists A, T, G, C or N

Wallace-rule Tm is applied to every length, so the 60-mer gets Tm 180 °C. For the primer containing N, GC% + AT% = 95.2%, because N counts toward length but not toward either percentage. I report these as observed and did not investigate them further

Silently dropped batch records were not tested. The reviewer reports from app.py that records with characters other than A/T/G/C/N, or with empty sequences, are skipped without a message; all 8 records in sample_primers.fasta were valid, so the only check is comparing 'Successfully processed N sequences' with the file's record count

I did not apply the Tm 50-60 °C / GC 40-60% cutoffs to the batch to make a keep/reject list, and I did not compare forward/reverse pair Tm for the GAPDH and TP53 pairs. The tool has no feature for either; it could only be done by reading the Data Table
I tested only the given 8-record FASTA; I did not try a 50+ record file or a .txt upload because no such test files were available
When I switched tabs the page reran and the Single Sequence results disappeared, while the input text stayed (screens/039.webp)
